literal.prompt: Какое событие 1917 года привело к отречению Николая II и падению монархии?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The prompt asks for the Russian 1917 event leading to Nicholas II’s abdication and the end of monarchy; answer labels are four named Russian political events from distinct dates/contexts. The President Library account links the February 1917 revolution to abdication and overthrow of autocracy (L50, L59-L60); its October account distinguishes the later Bolshevik seizure of power (L44, L50-L55); its Decembrist account dates that rising to 1825 (L40-L45); the retained Nicholas PDF also locates Bloody Sunday in January 1905 in St Petersburg (P17 L368-L374).
literalGroups.locator: President Library February page L50, L59-L60; October page L44-L55; Decembrist page L40-L45; Nicholas PDF P17 L368-L374 and P19 L402-L406.

literalGroups.literal: Февральская революция 1917 года привела к падению монархии в России. После неё возникло Временное правительство.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The February Revolution brought about Nicholas II’s abdication and the overthrow of autocracy; a Provisional Government was formed during the same revolutionary transition. The source describes formation on 2 (15) March and the late-evening abdication that date.
literalGroups.locator: President Library February page L57-L60; cross-check Nicholas PDF P19 L402-L406.

literalGroups.literal: Во время Февральской революции забастовки в Петрограде переросли во всеобщую политическую стачку, а затем — в вооружённое восстание.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note adds the event’s sequence: Petrograd strikes became a general political strike and then an armed uprising. This is a distinct, useful fact beyond naming the event or restating abdication/fall of monarchy.

literalGroups.literal: Октябрьская революция привела большевиков к власти в 1917 году.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The named October Revolution was the Bolsheviks’ seizure of power; the Provisional Government was overthrown and the Bolsheviks became the ruling party.
literalGroups.locator: President Library October page L44, L50-L55.

literalGroups.literal: Восстание декабристов произошло в Санкт-Петербурге в декабре 1825 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Decembrist armed rising occurred in St Petersburg on 14 (26) December 1825.

literalGroups.literal: Кровавое воскресенье — расстрел шествия рабочих в Санкт-Петербурге 9 января 1905 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: In St Petersburg, troops fired on the January 1905 workers’ procession; the page identifies it as Bloody Sunday and dates it 9 (22) January 1905.
literalGroups.locator: President Library Nicholas PDF P17 L368-L374.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.fullPrompt: Какое событие 1917 года привело к отречению Николая II и падению монархии?
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.note: Во время Февральской революции забастовки в Петрограде переросли во всеобщую политическую стачку, а затем — в вооружённое восстание.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: The standalone answer name «Февральская революция» is a valid nominative event title answering «Какое событие…?»; no agreement cue singles it out.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The February Revolution is the only listed event tied by the source to Nicholas II’s abdication and overthrow of autocracy. The revised note is true and useful: it adds the sequence from Petrograd strikes to political strike and armed uprising, rather than repeating the key.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.locator: President Library February page L50-L52 and L59-L60.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: The standalone answer name «Октябрьская революция» is a valid nominative event title, parallel in form and detail to «Февральская революция».
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: It is a plausible same-year political-event distractor, but the source places the Bolshevik seizure of power in October, after the monarchy had already fallen. correctNoteNewFact.fact: During the February Revolution, strikes in Petrograd grew into a general political strike and then an armed uprising. This process detail is additional to the prompt/key, which ask only for the event leading to abdication and monarchy’s fall.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Russian-speaking adults with broad school-level historical knowledge.
absoluteDifficulty.ground: The card tests recognition of the widely taught event that ended the Russian monarchy in 1917. It requires no rare date or terminology; the distractors are recognizable Russian political events, with the two 1917 revolutions providing a plausible distinction.
absoluteDifficulty.qualification: This is an editorial audience judgement under the pinned EASY definition, not a measured population survey.
